prior_record.name: Google African cloud region (Nairobi)
prior_record.note: First Google cloud region on the continent, targeted for 2028.

decisions.note: Removed unconfirmed Nairobi proposal from the active project register. Google states its first African region opened in Johannesburg on 2024-01-31. This does not establish a Nairobi project or its proposed 2028 opening.
Added the AI-tools comparison from p.41 with the city-survey scope. Methods on pp.9–10 limit interpretation; not national adoption.

The report labels ownership 75% on p.12, but its methodology describes selected urban/semi-urban smartphone users (pp.9–10). Withheld as a national ownership estimate until the sampling denominator and weights are clarified.
Primary report p.15 gives 88%, with a smartphone-user base of 9,944 for 2025. The rounded headline is not a share of all Nigerians. Kept as contextual evidence; no national ownership value inferred.
Company statement says USD300m financing target subject to agreements and approvals. Recorded separately from committed capital and project capex.

Open page read in full. Regulator-published device connections for two quarters, kept as device connections with the smartphone/feature-phone split preserved. Not a population or subscriber measure and not headline-eligible supplementary evidence.
Open page read in full. The cumulative teacher count is recorded; the 10,382-school Phase II target is a planned scope and is kept in the observation note, not as a delivered count.
Open page read in full. A ministerial workforce figure with no reference year or definition is kept as supplementary evidence with those limits stated; no national employment inference is drawn.
Open page read in full. Government export targets recorded as targets, separate from any measured export value.
Open page read in full. Two measured years of local mobile-device production recorded; the 2026 expectation and the demand range stay in the note rather than in the series.
Open page read in full. Training places recorded as announced capacity, with applications, eligibility and first-cohort counts kept in the note. No completion or employment claim.
Open page read in full. A signed memorandum of understanding is an announcement: recorded as announced training capacity, not delivered training.
Open page read in full. The awarded spectrum price and band allocations are recorded; no capacity, coverage or capex figure is claimed from them.

Open page read in full. The article attributes 'more than 23 million' Nigerians without meaningful internet access to unnamed industry figures and separately reports that the Federal Government's Project BRIDGE flags 'more than 33 million' as offline, without reconciling the two or defining 'meaningful access'; the summit's own theme refers to 'the next 25 million users'. No observation was recorded. Needed: the underlying NCC or Project BRIDGE dataset with its definition of access, reference date and geographic coverage.

Company press release read in full. Announces a Johannesburg colocation facility for the iGaming sector, said to be live in Q4 2026, with no capacity, investment, employment or site figure and no AI-specific workload described. Nothing comparable to a project register row could be recorded and no capacity may be inferred. Needed: a capacity or investment disclosure, or a dated operating confirmation, before it can be considered for the infrastructure register.

Reported programme launch. Benin hosted the programme; the other countries are explicitly named as participants' origins. The 190 places are a multinational cohort, not a count for each country or jobs created.
Announcement. Scheduled training in Lome. The stated 100 is a target; this article does not verify attendance, completion or employment.
Programme proposal. UNDP describes stakeholder consultations and accreditation work. The degree is proposed, not confirmed as accredited or delivering graduates.
Reported launch. Local reporting describes a launch and provider claims about access to legal information. Accuracy, usage and effects on legal services have not been independently measured.
Strategy preparation. The ministry reports discussions following a Blueprint workshop. This is strategy preparation, not evidence of adoption or completed deployment.
Reported workshop. Workshop in Windhoek involved institutions from both countries. Global UNESCO survey percentages are not national adoption estimates. Page updated 24 August 2026.

Research publication. Publisher summary covers Malawi, Rwanda, Togo, Zambia, Kenya and South Africa. Deployment, activation and operation are distinct stages; no GPU inventory or MW value is inferred from this page.

Research publication. Publisher description establishes report scope. It does not rank countries or demonstrate adoption or economic impact; individual policy claims require reading the underlying documents.
Reported summit. Organizer report from Yasmine Hammamet. A declaration and discussions do not establish implementation, investment delivered or national adoption.

Government progress report. Arabic ministry report distinguishes planned infrastructure/data actions, existing servers and GPUs, model progress and proposed training. No capacity, budget or employment outcome is inferred. This is the third coordination meeting on 21 September, a follow-up to the August roadmap and September committee-creation signals already retained.
Reported graduation. ENA reports a graduation ceremony after six months of training. Cohort size and jobs created are not given; broad official impact claims are not treated as measured outcomes.
Reported policy discussion. Mozambique is the participating regulator and Angola the host. Discussion of sandbox design is not proof that an operational AI sandbox has been launched.
Research and proposals. Organizer account of an economic forum and AI study. Suggested applications and a future roadmap are proposals; reported economic indicators are not attributed to AI.

Regional policy preparation. Eswatini is the meeting host. The statement is dated 16 September and posted 25 September. Regional strategy and regulatory instruments are future work, not enacted national law.

Reported soft launch. The ministry describes a trip planner and chatbot soft launch; analytics remain a later phase. Publication date is shown in the ministry news listing. No independent user or economic-impact measurement.

Government policy and pilot report. Presidency reports framework approval and teacher-coach and student-tutor pilots. These are limited pilots, not nationwide use or independently demonstrated learning gains.
Reported forum. Dakar is the host. The source discusses responsible AI in banking; it does not quantify deployment or financial-inclusion gains for Senegal or every UEMOA member.
Reported demonstration. Mauritius is the host; the other countries supplied visiting delegates. Participation does not establish that visiting parliaments deployed AI.

Reported investment priorities. Secondary reporting on policy priorities and proposed partnerships. Planned training and pilots are not completions; no new funded facility or operating capacity is established.

Interview with Polytech's founder reports about 50 AI-course graduates during 2026 to date. This is a provider claim, not independently audited, and not a count of jobs created. Exact course and graduation dates are unstated.
The commission reports a stakeholder workshop on preliminary readiness findings. This does not establish an adopted AI strategy, deployed systems or measured economic gains.

The ministry says AI helps triage the severity of photo-and-location reports for the water authority. No usage, model accuracy, water savings or independently evaluated impact is published in this announcement.

Voix du Togo seeks voice and text contributions for Kabye, Ewe and Moba, with UNDP support. Paid contribution tasks are not a count of permanent jobs. Wider language coverage and public-service access are ambitions, not established outcomes.

The ministerial account discusses possible AI use for administrative tasks and proposed bilateral cooperation. It does not demonstrate an AI deployment or signed implementation contract. The existing AIGLES payroll system is not reclassified as AI.

INTIC and INS report a five-year agreement for laboratory, digital-health and AI-sandbox cooperation. Facilities and sandbox implementation are prospective; the agreement is not proof of an operating AI system. This is distinct from the September regional sandbox discussion.

The programme partner describes a model supporting survey analysts in Kinyarwanda, English and French. Its 96% auto-coding result concerns one reported test, not national AI accuracy. Reported workflow savings do not establish layoffs; an enumerator app remains a future step.

The Mwando preprint describes support for four shiKomori varieties and an evaluation on 500 queries. This is author-reported research, not independently verified deployment, user adoption or economic impact. The country tag identifies the language context, not proof of operation throughout Comoros.

The call covers health, language processing, agriculture and environment, with an application deadline of 24 August 2026. It does not report successful applicants, completed training or jobs created. The historical call is no longer presented as an open opportunity.
